o1.biggest_strength: It follows the data tightly: Controllers/Heads of Finance at 50-300 person SaaS companies, timed to pricing-page changes, with no links and a clear expected reply-rate model.
o1.biggest_mistake: It uses the 9-to-4-day proof in step 1 and repeats it often; I would rather keep step 1 more focused on the pricing-change pain and use proof later.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the proof out of step 1, trim the repetition across steps, and make the Step 2 ask a little softer than a 20-minute walkthrough.

o2.biggest_strength: It picks the right segment and trigger, explains the list rules clearly, and gives a practical reply-rate expectation without overclaiming.
o2.biggest_mistake: The emails often have more than one ask and lean into SDR-style reply prompts like "reply yes" or "reply steps," which feels less like finance peer-to-peer copy.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Reduce each email to one clean question, remove the extra content offers unless those assets are ready, and make the copy sound more like a Controller talking to another finance leader.

reason: Output 1 is closer to something I could hand to the team tomorrow: sharper targeting, better use of the pilot data, and cleaner finance-led copy. Output 2 is solid, but the reply prompts and extra asks make it feel less polished and less on-brand.
